reason: Equivalent. `close` is the result of indexOf for the closing tag, searched from `bodyFrom`. Because every span begins after an opening `<script...>` tag, bodyFrom is never smaller than 8, so indexOf can only return -1 or a value of at least 8. It can never return 0, which is the single value that separates `< 0` from `<= 0`. No page can be written that tells the two apart. That an unclosed script is detected at all, and that it leaves nowhere safe to graft, is asserted directly in section 7.

The two versions differ only when lastEnd equals src.length exactly — a page whose final character is the last character of a closing script tag. In that case the original returns lastEnd and the mutant falls through to the next line, which returns src.length. Those are the same number, so the insertion point is identical and no test could distinguish them. That a page with no </body> appends after the last script is asserted in section 10.

reason: Equivalent. This picks the message off a caught parse error. A thrown SyntaxError is always a truthy object carrying a message, so both versions read e.message. For the only other possibility — a thrown null or undefined — the original short-circuits to the fallback text, and the mutant evaluates `e || e.message`, which is undefined and therefore falsy, so it reaches the same fallback. Both produce the identical reason string for every input. That a real parse failure is reported with its own message rather than a generic one is asserted in section 4.

The versions differ only for a value that is truthy but not an object — a string, a number, true, a function — which the original replaces with {} and the mutant keeps. Either way the next lines read o.marker, o.parse and o.parseModule off it, and none of those types carries any of those properties, so all three are undefined in both cases: the marker falls back to the banner line and the missing parser makes graft throw. That graft throws rather than skipping its check when no parser is supplied is asserted in section 9.

reason: Equivalent. This rejects a start position that is past the end of the document. The two versions differ only when the position equals the length exactly. The original returns it straight back; the mutant lets it through, and the walk then slices from the very end, which yields an empty string, matches none of the three patterns, and returns the same position because nothing was consumed. Both hand back the identical offset for every input. That a position past the end consumes nothing is asserted in section 13.

Equivalent in every reachable case. This is the runaway guard on the walk over consecutive injected blocks, and it only ever runs while blocks are still being consumed — the loop breaks the moment it meets anything it does not recognise. Sixty-four is far above any real run: the worst page found in the estate had three. One extra permitted iteration therefore changes nothing, because the loop has already broken long before. The guard exists so a malformed document cannot spin forever, and that property is unchanged either way.

Equivalent, for the same reason as the identical test in scriptSpans. The close offset is the result of indexOf for a closing tag, searched from a position that is already past an opening script tag, so it can only be -1 or a value well above zero. It can never be exactly 0, which is the single value separating the two comparisons. No document can be written that tells them apart. That a run whose inline script never closes stops the walk rather than consuming the rest of the file is what this line protects, and that behaviour is identical in both versions.
